text.p: Emilio Botin, chairman of leading Spanish bank Santander said he would not be pleased by a potential savings bank purchase in minority state-owned bank Argentaria, local media reported on Thursday.
In Turin, Italy, for the annual shareholder's meeting of Banco San Paolo, Botin said he would "look askance" at such a move.

Late last month, the president of the Spanish Confederation of Savings Banks (CECA), Braulio Medel, said some savings banks were interested in participating in the next state stake sale in Argentaria.

Argentaria, formed in 199, in a merger of six state-owned banks and savings banks and still 29.2 percent state-owned, is scheduled for further privatisation this year although no specific dates have been set.

In a separate interview with Spanish news agency EFE, Botin said "It's very important that Argentaria is an independent group...In Spain, there is already great concentration in banking and so no more is needed."
